accuracy.evidence: Checked against UK NC Y3 Rocks (fossils formed when things that have lived are trapped within rock) and BBC Bitesize KS2 fossils: die/bury, sediment layers, millions of years to rock, preserved shape (body or trace). Lab sort excludes plastic/metal non-fossils.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets: any old stone is a fossil; plastic toys/coins count; fossils form in days; footprints cannot be fossils; digging roughly is fine. Challenge feedback names each slip.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab is the fossil-formation sequence (bury → layers → rock → dig → sort). Cannot be reused for life cycles or melting by changing labels; the mechanism is deep-time burial in sediment.

lab_teaches.evidence: Doing the steps builds the causal chain; text confirms after each discovery. Sort step forces the living-thing criterion.

predictions.evidence: Predictions tempt 'left in the sun', 'one week', 'plastic dinosaur toy' — documented wrong first steps and time-scales the lab then disproves.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() messages name stone/toy/sun/paint/day/draw/metal slips with the specific reason, not a generic 'try again'.

readability.evidence: Kid lines use short sentences and concrete words (mud, shell, rock). Adult names NC Y3 and common mistakes without jargon piles.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid/adult sentence teaches the sequence or a mistake; no 'in this lesson' or journey padding.

mobile.evidence: Big lbtn twins for every canvas tap; young class; layout works at 390 px with stacked controls.

accessibility.evidence: Buttons mirror bury/layer/rock/dig/sort; live aria-label via say(); challenge uses role=group and status.

sources: BBC Bitesize KS2 How fossils are formed
